column1: # Phylogenetic marker gene panel, one row per target x marker.
# This table drives the whole marker workflow (code/analysis/11..16). Edit it
# rather than the scripts: add a row to add a locus, delete a row to drop one.
# WHY A PER-TARGET PANEL: 16S rRNA does not resolve Rickettsia to species and
# barely separates the Coxiella-like endosymbionts from C. burnetii. The
# discriminatory locus differs by genus (gltA/ompA/ompB/sca4 for Rickettsia,
# flaB for Borrelia, msp4 for Anaplasma, cox1/cytb for the piroplasms), so the
# panel is defined per target and every locus is searched independently. A
# target is NOT expected to yield every locus -- the assembly decides that.
#   target        must match a `taxon` in metadata/target_taxa.tsv
#   marker        short locus label; becomes part of every sequence name
#   marker_type   rrna    -> reference nucleotide seqs, found with blastn
#                 protein -> reference protein seqs, found with tblastn,
#   n_refs        how many reference sequences to fetch for searching
#   min_aln_len   minimum HSP length to keep a hit (bp for rrna, aa for protein)
#   min_pident    minimum percent identity to keep a hit
#   query         Entrez search term. Multiple alternatives may be separated by
#                 ' ||| ' -- they are tried in order until one returns hits, so
#                 a curated phrase can fall back to a looser one. These refs are
#                 used ONLY to locate and orient the locus; they are not the
#                 reference set for your tree, which you add by hand.
